source: Connected official PixelLab MCP tool declarations and read-only capability response

tools.name: mcp__pixellab__get_upload_url
tools.description:
Get a URL to upload a local image file to, without needing your API token.

Use it whenever you have an image on disk and a tool wants an image: send
the file with one curl, and pass the `upload:<id>` it returns to any
parameter that takes an image URL (image_urls, reference_image_url,
init_image_url, a style_image "url" ...). This avoids pasting base64 into a
tool call, which clients truncate and can corrupt. Free.

The URL works for 15 minutes and for any number of files. Uploads are kept
3 days. An animated GIF keeps all its frames.

PixelLab AI-powered pixel art generation service.

Use of this service is subject to PixelLab's Terms of Service:
https://pixellab.ai/termsofservice

This MCP server provides programmatic access to generate:
- Characters with multiple directional views
- Character animations
- Isometric tiles
- Top-down tilesets for game maps
- Sidescroller tilesets for platformer games

All generation operations are non-blocking and return job IDs for status tracking.
Requires PixelLab subscription (with credit fallback support).

**Pixel tools (free, exact, you are the artist)**: one command line, pixelart_workbench(argv=[...]), inspects, edits, draws and animates pixel art by your own decisions; combine it with the AI tools above. Start with pixelart_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start'], mode='low'|'high') — low acts directly with few tokens, high plans out loud and reviews every frame. Animated effects (spells, hits, explosions, auras): vfx_workbench(argv=['describe', 'start']) — same ids, exports to the user's My effects.

**Git access**: Clone and push game project source code with standard git.
Use `list_projects` to see your projects and their git clone URLs.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__get_upload_url(args: {}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

mcp__pixellab__wait_for_jobs
tools.description:
Wait for your running generations instead of sleeping and polling.

Returns as soon as min_finished (default 1) of your pending/processing jobs
finish, immediately when none are running, or at the timeout. Free. Then call
the matching get_* tool for the result; call wait_for_jobs again for the jobs
still running.

exec tool declaration:
```ts
declare const tools: { mcp__pixellab__wait_for_jobs(args: {
  // Return once this many of your running jobs have finished (or all of them, if fewer are running). 1 frees you to fill a slot the moment one opens; raise it for a large batch so one call covers several.
  min_finished?: number;
  // Give up waiting after this many seconds (jobs keep running). If your client times out the call itself (some stop a tool at ~60s), pass a value under that limit and call again.
  timeout_seconds?: number;
}): Promise<CallToolResult>; };
```

capability_response.name: Pro Flash
capability_response.grid_recovery: Creation recovers the pixel grid the model drew with Unzoom. An exact grid is kept; drift of at most one pixel is recovered on the expected grid. Images with a background must fill the canvas, so any other size is redrawn with image-to-pixel-art on the generated box only. Sprites without a background keep their own pixels, centred on the canvas, while the drawn pixel is close to the requested one; coarser or oversized sprites are redrawn. Experimental 16x16 creation always uses image-to-pixel-art. Editing and inpainting start at 32x32 and never use image-to-pixel-art conversion.

edit.reference_image_fit: native dimensions must fit the edit canvas

character.rotation_canvas: Native source padded to a square, minimum 32 pixels, aligned to four pixels.

object.rotation_canvas: Eight views use the square V3 canvas; one direction keeps the native size.

capability_response.style_reference_fit: native dimensions must fit the target canvas; smaller references are centered without resizing
